AI-Driven Discovery of Nodakenin as a Novel Molecular Glue Targeting the TRIM28-NR4A1-LCN2 Axis to Induce Ferroptosis in Melanoma.

Using AI-driven virtual screening, the authors identified the coumarin derivative Nodakenin as an inhibitor of the orphan nuclear receptor NR4A1, which is highly expressed in melanoma cells. Biochemical and structural analyses indicate that Nodakenin acts as a molecular glue along the TRIM28-NR4A1-LCN2 axis, triggering ferroptosis and thereby suppressing melanoma. This work nominates a new compound and a targetable vulnerability for melanoma therapy.

Molecular biomedicine 2026-11-21 Medium

Targeting protein degradation strategies in drug discovery: integrating PROTACs, ubiquitination biology, and AI-driven design.

This review examines targeted protein degradation as a therapeutic strategy, focusing on PROTACs that hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system to eliminate disease-causing proteins rather than merely inhibit them. It discusses key determinants of successful PROTAC translation—target degradability, E3 ligase selection, and linker design—and highlights how AI-driven approaches are being integrated into the design pipeline. The paper frames TPD as a convergence of ubiquitination biology, medicinal chemistry, and computational design.

canSAR 2026 is an updated public knowledgebase for cancer drug discovery that integrates large multidisciplinary datasets into a connected, navigable knowledge map. Artificial intelligence in basic and translational cardiovascular research.

This narrative review surveys artificial intelligence applications in basic and translational cardiovascular research, covering imaging, computational omics, mechanistic simulation, and drug discovery. It distinguishes genuine machine learning and deep learning contributions from routine bioinformatics and biophysical modeling, and evaluates study design, validation strategies, and strength of inference in representative studies.

Toll-Like Receptors in Mycoplasma Infections: Immunopathogenesis, Cheminformatics, and Machine Learning-Based Insights into TLR-Targeted Therapeutics.

This review examines how Toll-like receptors recognize Mycoplasma components such as lipoproteins, glycolipids, and CpG DNA, triggering NF-κB and MAPK signaling that can both clear infection and drive chronic inflammatory pathology. The authors integrate cheminformatics and machine learning approaches to identify and evaluate potential TLR-targeted therapeutic compounds. It synthesizes immunopathogenesis with computational drug-discovery strategies for Mycoplasma infections.

AI-powered virtual cells, digital twins and agentic AI are reshaping multi-omics, spatial biology and drug discovery.

This perspective argues that combining single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is enabling a new class of 'virtual cell' and 'digital twin' models that capture cellular dynamics, spatial context, and adaptive treatment responses, moving beyond static molecular snapshots. The authors frame agentic AI as a key driver of this shift and discuss its implications for multi-omics integration, spatial biology, and drug discovery workflows.

From static structures to conformational ensembles: Artificial intelligence for protein sampling and dynamics.

This review discusses how machine learning and AI are moving beyond static protein structure prediction toward modeling protein conformational ensembles and dynamics. The authors argue that fast, scalable ensemble representations could enable genome-scale studies of protein function with applications in drug discovery and protein engineering, though the challenges are much greater than single-structure prediction due to the broad timescales and complex relationships involved.

BioLM-Score: Language-Prior Conditioned Probabilistic Geometric Potentials for Protein-Ligand Scoring.

The paper introduces BioLM-Score, a protein-ligand scoring method that conditions a probabilistic geometric potential on pretrained biomolecular language model representations. It tests whether such language priors improve scoring performance across affinity prediction, pose selection, and virtual screening under a controlled geometric baseline. The work probes whether pretrained representations can mitigate poor generalization of geometric likelihood models when structural training coverage is limited.

A Machine Learning-Enhanced Ligand-Based Workflow Identifies Novel Cryptosporidium parvum Inhibitors.

The authors developed a ligand-based virtual screening workflow combining Thompson Sampling, a pharmacophore model, and a machine-learning classifier to search 51 million virtual compounds for new Cryptosporidium parvum inhibitors. This approach identified novel candidate compounds against the parasite that causes severe diarrheal disease, addressing the lack of effective treatments beyond nitazoxanide.

Learning inhibitor interactions from protein deep mutational scanning data and deep learning models.

This preprint benchmarks protein language models, geometric deep learning, and structure-based methods on their ability to predict how mutations in the MET kinase affect inhibitor responses, using deep mutational scanning data across 11 inhibitor conditions. The authors find that these models struggle to generalize to mutation-dependent drug responses, highlighting a key limitation for computational drug discovery. The work provides a systematic evaluation framework for assessing model performance beyond training distributions.

Who Knows Medicinal Chemistry? Expertise, Attrition, and the Dissolving Boundaries of a Craft.

This Viewpoint argues that medicinal chemistry expertise is largely tacit and poorly captured by binary possess-or-lack classifications, and that outcomes are dominated by attrition. As new modalities, AI, and cross-organizational collaboration dissolve disciplinary boundaries, the author proposes a more defensible way to measure expertise.

Democratizing Drug Discovery: A Scalable Open-Source Pipeline for Massive Specific Protein Target QSAR Modeling Using ChEMBL.

The authors present an open-source, automated pipeline that builds QSAR models at scale using ChEMBL data, generating 2263 predictive models across many protein targets with regression and classification approaches and strict quality control. The pipeline combines ErG and RDKit descriptors with Random Forest and XGBoost, tuned via Optuna, to make virtual screening more accessible. This democratizes AI-driven drug discovery by providing a reproducible, scalable alternative to proprietary tools.

Drug Design and Discovery: The Long Road From Hansch Analysis to Artificial Intelligence.

This review traces the historical evolution of QSAR (quantitative structure-activity relationships) from Hansch analysis to modern machine learning and AI applications in drug discovery. A Hybrid Ligand- and Structure-Based Drug Design Invoked through Square Attention in Protein-Ligand Transformer.

The paper introduces a hybrid ligand- and structure-based drug design approach using a protein-ligand Transformer with a novel 'square attention' mechanism, replacing the standard row-wise Softmax attention to better capture interactions between heterogeneous inputs (protein residues and ligand atoms). This is intended to improve binding affinity prediction while also identifying the specific amino acid residues and ligand atoms responsible for molecular interactions.

CB-Smart: A Cloud-Based Machine Learning Platform for Screening Cannabinoid Receptor Ligands.

CB-Smart is a cloud-based machine learning platform that predicts whether a compound binds to the cannabinoid receptors CB1 and CB2 and estimates its relative binding affinity. It was trained on curated experimentally validated ligands and GPCR decoys, offering a faster alternative to conventional structure-based virtual screening for cannabinoid drug discovery.

GAC-BiT-CNN: A Hybrid Generative Adversarial Capsule-Transformer-CNN Model with Fused Protein Language Model Embeddings for Methyltransferase Prediction.

The authors present GAC-BiT-CNN, a hybrid deep learning framework that combines generative adversarial capsule networks, a bidirectional transformer, and a CNN, using fused protein language model embeddings to predict methyltransferases from sequence. The model is motivated by the importance of MTs in epigenetic regulation and disease, and aims to improve computational identification of these enzymes for research and drug discovery.

ML-QSAR and Fragment Selectivity for the Identification of Fourth-Generation EGFRL858R/T790M/C797S Inhibitors.

The authors built an integrated computational pipeline combining machine-learning QSAR models (XGBoost with SHAP interpretation), fragment-level selectivity analysis, large-scale virtual screening of the ZINC database, and MD simulations to identify fourth-generation EGFR inhibitors targeting the L858R/T790M/C797S mutant. The models distinguished mutant from wild-type EGFR with good predictive accuracy, and fragment motifs were used to prioritize candidate compounds. This is a computational drug-discovery workflow with candidates proposed but not yet experimentally validated.

Computer-Aided Drug Design for Immunosuppressive Tumor Microenvironment Reprogramming: A Critical Review.

This critical review examines how computer-aided drug design (CADD) can be used to identify and test molecular interventions that reprogram the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment in solid tumors. It distinguishes observational AI predictions from actionable molecular hypotheses and outlines the experimental evidence needed to validate them, drawing on patient-derived models, spatial and multi-omics profiling, molecular simulation, and pharmacology.

Emerging Computational Advances in Simulating PCSK9 Variant Dynamics for Therapeutic Design Against Hypercholesterolemia.

This review surveys computational approaches for simulating the structural dynamics of PCSK9 variants, a key cholesterol-regulating protein targeted by approved drugs for hypercholesterolemia. It highlights how most therapeutic efforts have focused on the rigid catalytic domain that binds LDLR, while the flexible C-terminal cysteine-rich domain remains underexplored. The paper argues that emerging simulation methods could guide design of next-generation PCSK9 inhibitors.

A Machine-Learning Framework Integrating Frequency-Domain Spectral Features for Ligand Classification and Candidate Prioritization.

The authors introduce THz-FD, a feature-fusion framework that combines conventional molecular descriptors with terahertz frequency-domain spectral features to classify Na+/K+-ATPase ligands and prioritize candidates. Using Extra Trees, Random Forest, and SVM classifiers, they show that adding frequency-domain information can improve ligand classification and retrospective ranking. The work suggests spectral behavior as a complementary signal for AI-assisted drug discovery.

Integrating Artificial Intelligence with High-Throughput Biological Testing for Antimicrobial Drug Discovery.

This review examines how AI has been combined with high-throughput screening and prospective biological testing in antibacterial drug discovery.
